example: examples/deepseek-v4-pro (structure only; this page is the image example)

items.note: The H1 is exactly 'GPT Image 2 API'. The title starts with 'GPT Image 2 API' and ends with '| ZenMux'. The title, meta description, H1 and opening paragraph all name GPT Image 2. Everything the title and meta list is answered on the page: providers, token rates, billing items, sizes, reference images, 10K context, Python/cURL examples, alternatives and FAQ.

M1 says both providers list the same prices and that default routing sends each request to OpenAI or Azure. M1, M2 and the FAQ all give $8 image input, $30 image output and $5 prompt. M3 uses openai/gpt-image-2, the ID shown in M1. M4 scopes the capabilities that differ by provider (Gemini-protocol reference images).
M1 says the serving provider and its version vary by request, and only reports which aliases ZenMux and OpenAI list. M2 gives each provider row a Served version of Not verified.

Nothing uses $0 or 100% as a placeholder. Missing values appear as Not published / Not verified in their table cells (OpenAI max output, per-image price, served version, reference-image maximum). M5 and M6 are hidden.

Checked across modules: prices ($8/$30/$2/$5/$1.25), context 10K, max output, aliases, size rules (3840 px, 16 px, 3:1, 655,360–8,294,400), quality values, images per request, streaming status and the M7 estimate table against its 'Choose…' sentences (GPT Image 1.5 lower at 1024x1024 medium/high; GPT Image 2 lower in the other four combinations). None of them conflict. The cache-read rates sit beside OpenAI's attributed caveat, and the two statements are attributed to different sources, so this is not a self-contradiction.
The primary CTA reads 'Get your API key', which is the same wording as the reference examples. The secondary CTA is 'Try the API'. There is no Chat CTA.

All three examples call the Images API (/images/generations, images.generate) and read the key from $ZENMUX_API_KEY. None contains a real key. They use openai/gpt-image-2, the ID in M1, and the M3 prose explains that ZenMux's guide uses the alias gpt-image-2.

The anchors are model names or guide topics. The related models are same-task image models: GPT Image 1.5 (also the same series) and Qwen Image 2.0. The Sunset Gemini 3 Pro Image Preview link was removed. Links are site-relative paths; checking that they resolve is site acceptance.

Each shown module carries facts specific to GPT Image 2: per-provider max output, the fee-item table, the alias explanation, protocol-scoped capabilities with the streaming conflict, the size rules, and the 1.5-versus-2 estimate trade-off.

Every question the example covers is answered here too: what the model is, price and its conditions, providers, how to call it, capabilities and limits, alternatives and FAQ. Performance is correctly hidden: perf.azure.latency does not qualify under IMG-5. The example's FAQ also has a 'Which revision will I get?' question. This FAQ has none, but the revision question is answered in M1 and M2 (version.alias.zenmux, version.snapshot.openai), so it is not a coverage gap.
Both endpoints (openai, azure) are active in facts.json.

fact-check-report.md says the live API test was skipped by the user's decision on 2026-10-30. No call that returned a real image has been recorded, and the model ID (openai/gpt-image-2 or the alias gpt-image-2) has not been confirmed on /images/generations.

Shown: sizes (ZenMux examples plus OpenAI's four rules), the reference-image maximum as Not published in its M1 cell, the 50MB edit limit, images per request (1-10 on the Gemini protocol), and the billing items. Context and max output stay because billing is per token. The Images-protocol maximum for n is a ledger gap (max-n) and only appears in prose. An M1 row could show it as a label, but its absence is not a quotable failure.
Max output is shown per provider: 'Azure: 10,000 tokens; OpenAI: Not published'. Context is the same for both (10K).

The billing-items rows use ZenMux's fee-item codes (image_output, image_input, image_input_cache, prompt, input_cache_read). The Per image row shows Not published. The M7 per-image figures are labelled as OpenAI estimates, not as a ZenMux price.

Capabilities are scoped by protocol: the OpenAI Images protocol versus the Google Gemini (Vertex AI) protocol. The ledger shows the model's suitable_api as images,imagen only. Where they conflict on streaming, the page shows both ZenMux's listing and OpenAI's statement and marks it Not verified.
M5 is hidden. The Azure 99.5 s latency cell and 72.9 tps figure appear nowhere in the published text. The 'up to 2 minutes' line was removed.
M3 says 'ZenMux's Images guide uses the alias `gpt-image-2` in its generation examples'.
